<!--
The network analysis itself. This file is the single source for three
notebooks, which differ only in which predictability nodes they keep:

  network-analysis.qmd                     drop_var <- NULL         (15 nodes)
  sensitivity/network-no-varloss.qmd       drop_var <- "var_loss"   (14 nodes)
  sensitivity/network-no-meanloss.qmd      drop_var <- "mean_loss"  (14 nodes)

Each parent sets `drop_var` and then includes this file. Nothing below names
mean_loss or var_loss directly; the code works from `pred_vars` (retained) and
`focal` (the first retained node). See the `resolve-drop` chunk.

The leading underscore keeps Quarto's project render from treating this as a
document in its own right, and include paths are relative to the parent, so the
sensitivity notebooks include `../_network-body.qmd`.
-->

# Section 1. Setup and Data Preparation

```{r}
#| label: setup

library(tidyverse)  # always
library(psych)
library(corrplot)
library(qgraph)      # visualization
library(bootnet)     # edge-weight accuracy CIs + group viz networks
library(igraph)
library(EGAnet)      # estimation, communities, network loadings, network.compare
library(lavaan)

# NOTE: EGAnet's signatures have shifted across 2.x releases. Using EGAnet 2.4.1.
```

```{r}
#| label: resolve-drop

# `drop_var` is set by the parent notebook before this body is included. 
# NULL keeps the full battery (the main analysis); a variable name holds that one
# predictability node out (a sensitivity run). Everything downstream works from
# `pred_vars` (what is retained) and `focal` (the first retained node) instead
# of naming mean_loss or var_loss, so the three notebooks differ only here.
stopifnot(exists("drop_var"))
pred_all <- c("mean_loss", "var_loss")
stopifnot(is.null(drop_var) ||
          (length(drop_var) == 1 && drop_var %in% pred_all))

pred_vars <- setdiff(pred_all, drop_var)
focal <- pred_vars[1]

# Sensitivity runs write to their own directory under a run-specific prefix.
if (is.null(drop_var)) {
  fig_dir <- "fig"
  fig_prefix <- ""
} else {
  fig_dir <- "fig/sensitivity"
  fig_prefix <- paste0("no-", gsub("_", "", drop_var), "_")
}
dir.create(fig_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
fig_path <- function(stem) file.path(fig_dir, paste0(fig_prefix, stem))

# Figure export, matching the Study 1 helper in
# src/1-predictability-benchmark/_viz_helpers.R: an embedded-font vector PDF
# plus a 400 dpi PNG for contexts that cannot place vector art.
#
# cairo_pdf() rather than grDevices::pdf(). The default device does not embed
# its fonts, naming Helvetica and leaving the viewer to substitute, which fails
# the "all fonts embedded" check most print submissions apply; it is also
# Latin-1 only, so it silently rewrites en dashes and arrows as hyphens and
# drops a Greek delta outright.
#
# Study 1's helper takes a ggplot. The network figures here are base graphics
# (qgraph, bootnet), which draw as a side effect and cannot be replayed from a
# saved object, so this one takes a drawing function and calls it once per
# device instead.
FIG_DPI <- 400

save_base_fig <- function(stem, width, height, draw) {
  pdf_path <- fig_path(paste0(stem, ".pdf"))
  png_path <- fig_path(paste0(stem, ".png"))
  render <- function() {
    out <- draw()
    # bootnet's plot methods return a ggplot, which reaches the device only when
    # printed. qgraph draws directly and returns its object, so printing that
    # would dump a list to the console.
    if (inherits(out, "ggplot")) print(out)
    invisible(NULL)
  }
  grDevices::cairo_pdf(pdf_path, width = width, height = height)
  render(); grDevices::dev.off()
  grDevices::png(png_path, width = width, height = height, units = "in",
                 res = FIG_DPI, type = "cairo")
  render(); grDevices::dev.off()
  cat("Saved", pdf_path, "+", png_path, "\n")
}

n_cores <- parallel::detectCores() - 1

cat("Held out:", if (is.null(drop_var)) "nothing (full battery)" else drop_var, "\n")
cat("Predictability nodes retained:", paste(pred_vars, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Figures ->", fig_path("*.pdf"), "| bootstrap cores:", n_cores, "\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: load-data

# ellipse_metrics.csv carries the 16 linguistic features + ELLIPSE scores +
# predictability (mean_loss, var_loss) from the Study 1 benchmark model
# (OLMo-2 1B base, window 8). All networks below use Spearman correlations.
df_raw <- read.csv("data/ellipse/ellipse_metrics.csv")

cat("Raw data:", nrow(df_raw), "rows x", ncol(df_raw), "columns\n")
```

::: {.callout-note}
## A note on clauses per T-unit

`clauses_per_tunit` (C/T) is computed and retained in the metrics table but is
**not entered into the network**. On this corpus it does not measure
subordination; it measures punctuation.

The T-unit is the only denominator in the battery that depends on sentence
segmentation, and spaCy segments on punctuation. An unpunctuated run-on has
multiple independent clauses that are treated as subordinate by the parser.

- C/T correlates −0.205 with Overall proficiency across all essays
- But, correlates only −0.014 among well-punctuated essays (8--25 words per
  mark, *n* = 3,590).

The entire association is the confound.
:::

```{r}
#| label: select-features

# Assemble the feature set: 15 variables, less any held-out predictability node.
#
# The three syntactic indices (src/features/syntactic.py) sample distinct
# subconstructs rather than accumulating redundant omnibus measures (Norris &
# Ortega, 2009; Bulté & Housen, 2012): length at the clausal level (MLC), and
# phrasal elaboration and phrasal coordination at the NP level (CN/C, CP/C).
# All three are L2SCA indices (Lu, 2010, 2011), so the battery is
# comparable to the large body of work using that tool, though the measures
# share a denominator, so local dependence is expected.
#
# Three further indices are in the CSV but deliberately NOT entered:
#   - `clauses_per_tunit`  -- a punctuation index here; see the note above.
#   - `deps_per_clause`    -- (Kyle & Crossley, 2018) indexes the same
#                             clausal-length subconstruct as MLC, which is the
#                             far more widely reported measure.
#   - `deps_per_nominal`   -- (Kyle & Crossley, 2018) behaved as an island,
#                             loading -.098 on its own community and
#                             correlating ~.00 with every ELLIPSE subscore.
feature_vars <- c(
  # Lexical (4)
  "mtld", "lexical_density", "log_mean_token_freq", "mean_word_length",
  # Syntactic (3)
  "mean_length_of_clause",
  "complex_nominals_per_clause", "coord_phrases_per_clause",
  # Phraseological (3)
  "amod_mi", "dobj_mi", "advmod_mi",
  # Cohesion (3)
  "content_word_overlap", "connective_density", "sentence_similarity",
  # Predictability (2, less whatever `drop_var` holds out)
  pred_vars
)

df_features <- df_raw[, feature_vars]
```

```{r}
#| label: missing-data

# Report missingness. The few missing values are structural: dependency-MI
# features (amod/dobj/advmod) are undefined for bigrams unseen in the Dolma
# reference corpus, and content_word_overlap / sentence_similarity are undefined
# for single-sentence essays. Rather than listwise-delete (which biases the
# sample toward "typical" essays), we retain every essay and use
# pairwise-complete correlations throughout (Isvoranu & Epskamp, 2023).
missing_counts <- colSums(is.na(df_features))
cat("Missing values per variable (retained; handled pairwise):\n")
print(missing_counts[missing_counts > 0])
cat("\nEssays retained:", nrow(df_features),
    "(", sum(!complete.cases(df_features)), "have >=1 pairwise-handled NA)\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: residualize-on-prompt

# Residualize every variable on writing prompt to remove systematic
# prompt-driven variance. na.action = na.exclude keeps each residual vector
# full length with NA left in the originally-missing positions, so the
# downstream pairwise-complete correlations can use every available essay.
df_net <- df_features
r2_values <- numeric(ncol(df_features))
names(r2_values) <- names(df_features)

for (var in names(df_features)) {
  fit <- lm(df_features[[var]] ~ factor(df_raw$prompt), na.action = na.exclude)
  df_net[[var]] <- residuals(fit)
  r2_values[var] <- summary(fit)$r.squared
}

cat("R² (variance explained by prompt) per variable:\n")
r2_df <- data.frame(Variable = names(r2_values), R2 = round(r2_values, 4))
r2_df <- r2_df[order(-r2_df$R2), ]
print(r2_df, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Local dependence screening (UVA)

The syntactic battery is not independent by construction. All three indices
share the clause as a denominator, and MLC's numerator (the word count)
necessarily includes the postmodifiers that make a nominal complex and the
conjuncts that make a coordinate phrase, so MLC is structurally entangled with
CN/C and CP/C.

Unique Variable Analysis (Christensen, Garrido & Golino, 2023) quantifies it via
weighted topological overlap. This section **reports** wTO and does not act on
it. No variable is removed or combined here, and the conventional .25 cutoff is
printed only as a reference line. Where a pair looks dependent, the reading of
that pair's shared community is qualified in the discussion instead of the pair
being pruned.

```{r}
#| label: uva-screen

# Screen on the residualized data, since that is what every network below uses,
# with the same pairwise missing-data handling as every other estimate here.
# reduce = FALSE: report the overlap only. Nothing downstream consumes this.
uva <- UVA(data = df_net, cut.off = 0.25, reduce = FALSE,
           na.data = "pairwise", verbose = FALSE)

wto_pairs <- uva$wto$pairwise
wto_pairs <- wto_pairs[order(-wto_pairs$wto), ]

cat("Highest weighted topological overlap:", round(max(wto_pairs$wto), 3), "\n")
cat("Pairs at or above the .25 reference line:",
    sum(wto_pairs$wto >= 0.25), "of", nrow(wto_pairs), "\n\n")

cat("Top 12 pairs by wTO (reported, not acted on):\n")
print(head(wto_pairs, 12), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: define-battery

# Every variable in feature_vars enters the network; UVA above is diagnostic.
syntactic_battery <- c("mean_length_of_clause",
                       "complex_nominals_per_clause", "coord_phrases_per_clause")

cat("Variables entering the network:", ncol(df_net), "\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: define-groups

# Theoretical groupings (construct membership).
construct_members <- list(
  Lexical        = c("mtld", "lexical_density", "log_mean_token_freq", "mean_word_length"),
  Syntactic      = syntactic_battery,
  Phraseological = c("amod_mi", "dobj_mi", "advmod_mi"),
  Cohesion       = c("content_word_overlap", "connective_density", "sentence_similarity"),
  Predictability = pred_vars
)

# Canonical node order, shared by the full-sample and proficiency-group networks.
node_order <- feature_vars

# Short labels for plotting
short_labels <- c(
  mtld = "MTLD",
  lexical_density = "LexDen",
  log_mean_token_freq = "TokFreq",
  mean_word_length = "WordLen",
  clauses_per_tunit = "C/T",
  mean_length_of_clause = "MLC",
  complex_nominals_per_clause = "CN/C",
  coord_phrases_per_clause = "CP/C",
  amod_mi = "AmodMI",
  dobj_mi = "DobjMI",
  advmod_mi = "AdvMI",
  content_word_overlap = "CWO",
  connective_density = "ConnDen",
  sentence_similarity = "SentSim",
  mean_loss = "Loss",
  var_loss = "VarLoss"
)

net_labels <- short_labels[node_order]

# Which a priori construct each node belongs to. Shape encodes this (see the
# `define-shapes` chunk); colour is reserved for the empirically derived EGA
# communities, which are not known until Section 3.
node_construct <- rep(NA_character_, length(node_order))
names(node_construct) <- node_order
for (g in names(construct_members)) {
  node_construct[construct_members[[g]]] <- g
}
node_construct <- node_construct[node_order]
```

```{r}
#| label: define-shapes

# --- Visual encoding: SHAPE = a priori theoretical construct ----------------
# Colour goes to the empirical EGA communities (Section 3) because readers go to
# colour first and will take whatever it encodes to be the discovered grouping.
# qgraph ships a few poor quality shapes. Both the rhombus and the 5-pointed
# star are supplied as custom polygons

shape_polygons <- list(
  rhombus = list(x = c(0, 1, 0, -1), y = c(1, 0, -1, 0)),
  star = local({
    ang <- seq(pi / 2, pi / 2 + 2 * pi, length.out = 11)[1:10]
    list(x = rep(c(1, 0.6), 5) * cos(ang), y = rep(c(1, 0.6), 5) * sin(ang))
  })
)

# Ordered most- to least-distinguishable at small sizes
shape_pool <- c("circle", "square", "triangle", "rhombus", "star")

# Shapes with less usable interior than a circle are drawn larger so that the
shape_scale <- c(circle = 1, square = 1, triangle = 1.3, rhombus = 1.15, star = 1.4)

# Plotting-character equivalents, for the shape half of the legend
shape_pch <- c(circle = 21, square = 22, triangle = 24, rhombus = 23, star = 8)

# One shape per theoretical construct, in the order the constructs are declared.
stopifnot(length(construct_members) <= length(shape_pool))
construct_shapes <- setNames(shape_pool[seq_along(construct_members)],
                             names(construct_members))
node_shapes <- unname(construct_shapes[node_construct])

# Node sizes follow the shape, so they are fixed here rather than per-figure.
node_vsize <- unname(7.5 * shape_scale[node_shapes])
```

# Section 3. Network Estimation (EBICglasso) and Community Detection

```{r}
#| label: estimate-network

# Estimate Gaussian Graphical Model (EBICglasso) on Spearman correlations
# (Isvoranu & Epskamp, 2023).
#
# This is the same network produced by EGA(), using the same estimator.
# The two graphs are numerically identical once lambda.min.ratio matches
# (qgraph defaults to 0.01, EGAnet to 0.1). The `ega` chunk asserts it.
# Two objects exist only because bootnet() and EGAnet each need their own class.
network <- estimateNetwork(df_net, default = "EBICglasso", tuning = 0.5,
                           corMethod = "spearman", missing = "pairwise",
                           lambda.min.ratio = 0.1)

cat("Network estimated with", ncol(network$graph), "nodes\n")
cat("Non-zero edges:", sum(network$graph[upper.tri(network$graph)] != 0),
    "out of", sum(upper.tri(network$graph)), "possible\n")
cat("Sparsity:", round(1 - mean(network$graph[upper.tri(network$graph)] != 0), 3), "\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: adjacency-matrix
#| tbl-cap: "Weighted adjacency matrix (partial correlations)"

adj_mat <- round(network$graph, 3)
colnames(adj_mat) <- short_labels[colnames(adj_mat)]
rownames(adj_mat) <- short_labels[rownames(adj_mat)]
print(adj_mat)
```

```{r}
#| label: ega

# Exploratory Graph Analysis: the empirically derived community structure.
# Estimated here rather than in Section 6 because every network plot from
# Section 4 onward colours its nodes by community.
ega_result <- EGA(df_net, corr = "spearman", model = "glasso",
                  algorithm = "walktrap", na.data = "pairwise",
                  plot.EGA = FALSE)

# The communities are detected on the same graph that Sections 4, 5 and 7
# report. Asserted rather than assumed, since it rests on package defaults.
stopifnot(max(abs(network$graph -
                  ega_result$network[colnames(network$graph),
                                     colnames(network$graph)])) < 1e-10)

cat("Number of communities detected:", ega_result$n.dim, "\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: community-aesthetics

# --- Visual encoding: COLOUR = empirical EGA community ----------------------
# The full-sample community assignment is reused for every network plot,
# including the proficiency-group panels in Section 9.
#
# Hues are the Okabe-Ito qualitative set, lightened toward white so that the
# dark node labels stay legible on the fill. Lightening preserves the hue
# separation that makes the set colour-vision-deficiency safe.
lighten <- function(hex, toward_white = 0.40) {
  v <- col2rgb(hex)[, 1]
  v <- round(v + toward_white * (255 - v))
  rgb(v[["red"]], v[["green"]], v[["blue"]], maxColorValue = 255)
}
color_pool <- vapply(c("#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#CC79A7", "#0072B2"),
                     lighten, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)

comm_ids <- sort(unique(ega_result$wc))
comm_n <- as.integer(table(factor(ega_result$wc, levels = comm_ids)))
stopifnot(length(comm_ids) <= length(color_pool))
community_colors <- setNames(
  color_pool[seq_along(comm_ids)],
  paste0("Community ", comm_ids, " (", comm_n, ")")
)
node_colors <- unname(community_colors[match(ega_result$wc[node_order], comm_ids)])

cat("Construct (shape) x EGA community (colour):\n")
print(table(Construct = factor(node_construct, levels = names(construct_members)),
            Community = ega_result$wc[node_order]))
cat("\nPer-node assignment:\n")
print(data.frame(
  Variable  = unname(net_labels),
  Construct = unname(node_construct),
  Community = unname(ega_result$wc[node_order])
), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-helpers

# A spring layout places strongly connected nodes almost on top of each other.
# With the full battery, Loss and VarLoss have a partial correlation near .7 and
# land within a node width of each other. This nudges any overlapping pair apart
# while holding every node `radius_scale` converts qgraph's `vsize` into
# the half-width of a node in plot coordinates.
relax_overlap <- function(co, vsize, iter = 600, pad = 1.10, radius_scale = 0.019) {
  r <- vsize * radius_scale
  lim <- 1 - r
  n <- nrow(co)
  for (it in seq_len(iter)) {
    moved <- FALSE
    for (i in seq_len(n - 1)) {
      for (j in (i + 1):n) {
        d <- co[j, ] - co[i, ]
        dist <- sqrt(sum(d^2))
        need <- pad * (r[i] + r[j])
        if (dist < need) {
          if (dist < 1e-8) { d <- c(1e-3, 0); dist <- 1e-3 }
          push <- 0.55 * (need - dist) / 2
          u <- d / dist
          co[i, ] <- co[i, ] - u * push
          co[j, ] <- co[j, ] + u * push
          moved <- TRUE
        }
      }
    }
    co[, 1] <- pmax(pmin(co[, 1], lim), -lim)
    co[, 2] <- pmax(pmin(co[, 2], lim), -lim)
    if (!moved) break
  }
  # Centre, then expand by a single factor so the graph fills the frame instead
  # of sitting in a band. One factor for both axes: a per-axis rescale would
  # stretch the layout and misrepresent the distances the spring layout encodes.
  co <- sweep(co, 2, c(mean(range(co[, 1])), mean(range(co[, 2]))))
  headroom <- 1 - max(r)
  scale <- min(headroom / max(abs(co[, 1])), headroom / max(abs(co[, 2])))
  co * max(1, scale)
}

# Spring coordinates for one graph, already de-overlapped
spring_coords <- function(graph, seed = 42) {
  set.seed(seed)
  qg <- qgraph(graph, layout = "spring", vsize = node_vsize, DoNotPlot = TRUE)
  relax_overlap(qg$layout, node_vsize)
}

# Legend in its own panel so it doesn't overlap the graph. Three blocks:
# colour (the primary reading), shape (secondary), edge style (sign).
draw_network_legend <- function(cex = 0.82, swatches = community_colors) {
  op <- par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
  on.exit(par(op))
  plot.new()
  plot.window(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1))
  legend(0, 0.98, legend = names(community_colors), pch = 22,
         pt.bg = unname(swatches), col = "grey45", pt.cex = 1.8,
         cex = cex, bty = "n", title = "EGA community (colour)",
         title.adj = 0, y.intersp = 1.3)
  legend(0, 0.70, legend = names(construct_shapes),
         pch = unname(shape_pch[construct_shapes]), pt.bg = "grey92",
         col = "grey10", pt.lwd = 1.6, pt.cex = 1.8, cex = cex, bty = "n",
         title = "Construct (shape)", title.adj = 0, y.intersp = 1.3)
  legend(0, 0.34, legend = c("positive", "negative"), lty = c(1, 2),
         lwd = 2.4, col = "grey25", cex = cex, bty = "n",
         title = "Partial correlation", title.adj = 0, y.intersp = 1.3)
}

# Single entry point for every network figure.
#
# `minimum` hides edges below |.05| and `cut` gives full width and saturation to
# edges above |.10|. The complete weighted adjacency matrix is printed above, so
# nothing is lost, only decluttered.
# `negDashed` makes edge sign readable in black and white.
plot_network <- function(graph, coords, title = "", legend = TRUE,
                         minimum = 0.05, cut = 0.10, color = node_colors,
                         posCol = "#2166AC", negCol = "#B2182B",
                         swatches = community_colors, ...) {
  if (legend) graphics::layout(matrix(1:2, nrow = 1), widths = c(1, 0.32))
  qg <- qgraph(graph,
               layout = coords,
               rescale = FALSE,
               labels = net_labels,
               color = color,
               shape = node_shapes,
               polygonList = shape_polygons,
               vsize = node_vsize,
               borders = TRUE,
               border.width = 2.6,
               border.color = "grey10",
               label.scale.equal = TRUE,
               label.color = "grey5",
               negDashed = TRUE,
               minimum = minimum,
               cut = cut,
               esize = 10,
               legend = FALSE,
               posCol = posCol,
               negCol = negCol,
               title = title,
               title.cex = 1.2,
               # qgraph's `mar` pads the [-1, 1] box in tenths; keep it tight so
               # the graph fills the panel, with extra headroom for the title.
               mar = c(2, 2, 4, 2),
               ...)
  if (legend) {
    draw_network_legend(swatches = swatches)
    graphics::layout(1)
  }
  invisible(qg)
}
```

# Section 4. Network Visualization

Node **colour** encodes the empirically derived EGA community. That is the
primary reading. Colour is the channel readers go to first, so it carries the
grouping that the data produced rather than the one assumed going in. Node
**shape** is the a priori theoretical construct. Nodes whose shape disagrees
with the colours around them are the cases where the data depart from the a
priori grouping. Solid edges are positive partial correlations, dashed edges
negative.

```{r}
#| label: network-spring
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   GGM network (spring layout, Fruchterman-Reingold). Colour = EGA community,
#|   shape = theoretical construct; edges below |.05| omitted.
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 8.5

spring_layout <- spring_coords(network$graph)

plot_network(network$graph, spring_layout,
             title = "ELLIPSE feature network (EBICglasso)")
```

```{r}
#| label: save-spring-plot
#| include: false

save_base_fig("network_spring", width = 13, height = 8.5, draw = function() {
  plot_network(network$graph, spring_layout,
               title = "ELLIPSE feature network (EBICglasso)")
})
```

```{r}
#| label: network-circle
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   GGM network (circle layout). Colour = EGA community, shape = theoretical
#|   construct; edges below |.05| omitted.
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 10

circle_layout <- local({
  ang <- seq(pi / 2, pi / 2 - 2 * pi, length.out = length(node_order) + 1)[-1]
  cbind(0.82 * cos(ang), 0.82 * sin(ang))
})

plot_network(network$graph, circle_layout,
             title = "ELLIPSE feature network, circle layout")
```

# Section 6. Community Structure (EGA)

`ega_result` is estimated in Section 3 (its communities drive the node colours
throughout); this section reports it.

```{r}
#| label: ega-assignments

cat("Number of communities detected:", ega_result$n.dim, "\n")
cat("\nCommunity assignments:\n")

# Show assignments with short labels
assignments <- data.frame(
  Variable = short_labels[names(ega_result$wc)],
  Full_name = names(ega_result$wc),
  Community = ega_result$wc
)
print(assignments %>% arrange(Community))
```

```{r}
#| label: ega-predictability

# Where each retained predictability node ended up. This is the whole point of
# the sensitivity runs, so it is pulled out rather than left buried in the full
# assignment table above.
for (v in pred_vars) {
  comm <- unname(ega_result$wc[v])
  members <- names(ega_result$wc)[ega_result$wc == comm]
  cat(unname(short_labels[[v]]), "-> Community", comm, "\n")
  cat("  Members:", paste(unname(short_labels[members]), collapse = ", "), "\n")
  cat("  With the dependency-MI indices:",
      all(c("amod_mi", "dobj_mi", "advmod_mi") %in% members), "\n\n")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: net-loadings
#| tbl-cap: "Revised network loadings (standardized)"

# Network loadings (Christensen, Golino, Abad & Garrido, 2025): confound-adjusted
# node importance that splits strength by community and adjusts for community
# size and sign.
# Effect-size guides: ~0.20 small, ~0.35 moderate, ~0.50 large.

nl <- net.loads(ega_result, loading.method = "revised")$std

nl_df <- as.data.frame(round(nl, 3))
nl_df$Variable <- short_labels[rownames(nl)]
nl_df <- nl_df %>% select(Variable, everything())
cat("Standardized network loadings (nodes x communities):\n")
print(nl_df, row.names = FALSE)

cat("\nPredictability network loadings:\n")
print(nl_df %>% filter(Variable %in% short_labels[pred_vars]), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: boot-ega
#| fig-cap: "Bootstrap EGA: stability of community assignments"

# NOT REPRODUCIBLE ACROSS RENDERS, despite the seed. bootEGA and the two
# bootnet calls below run their resampling in parallel worker processes, and
# neither seeds those workers from the master's RNG state, so set.seed() here
# fixes nothing that happens inside them.
set.seed(42)
boot_ega <- bootEGA(df_net, iter = 500,
                    corr = "spearman",
                    model = "glasso",
                    algorithm = "walktrap",
                    na.data = "pairwise",
                    type = "parametric",
                    verbose = FALSE)

cat("Modal number of communities across bootstraps:",
    as.numeric(names(sort(table(boot_ega$n.dim), decreasing = TRUE))[1]), "\n")

cat("\nDistribution of the number of communities across bootstraps:\n")
print(round(boot_ega$frequency, 3))

dim_stab <- dimensionStability(boot_ega, verbose = FALSE)

cat("\nStructural consistency (proportion of bootstraps in which each",
    "\nempirical community is exactly recovered):\n")
print(round(dim_stab$dimension.stability$structural.consistency, 3))

cat("\nItem stability (proportion of bootstraps in which each node is",
    "\nassigned to its empirical community):\n")
item_stab <- dim_stab$item.stability$item.stability$empirical.dimensions
names(item_stab) <- short_labels[names(item_stab)]
print(round(sort(item_stab), 3))
```

## Which communities merge when a bootstrap returns fewer

Structural consistency says *how often* a community is recovered but not *what
happens to it* when it is not. `bootEGA` keeps every bootstrap's membership
vector, so the merge pattern is recoverable without re-resampling.

```{r}
#| label: boot-merge-pattern

# `boot.wc` is iterations x nodes, but its columns are named V01..Vnn in the
# original column order rather than by variable, so the names are restored
# positionally. Asserted rather than assumed.
boot_wc <- boot_ega$boot.wc
stopifnot(ncol(boot_wc) == length(ega_result$wc))
colnames(boot_wc) <- names(ega_result$wc)

emp_ids <- sort(unique(ega_result$wc))
fewer <- which(boot_ega$boot.ndim < ega_result$n.dim)

# Each empirical community is mapped to the bootstrap community that most of its
# members landed in. Empirical communities sharing one bootstrap community are
# the ones that merged, so the signature "1+4 | 2 | 3" reads as community 4
# absorbed into community 1 with 2 and 3 intact.
merge_pattern <- vapply(fewer, function(i) {
  bw <- setNames(as.integer(boot_wc[i, ]), colnames(boot_wc))
  landed <- vapply(emp_ids, function(k) {
    v <- bw[names(ega_result$wc)[ega_result$wc == k]]
    v <- v[!is.na(v)]
    if (!length(v)) NA_integer_
    else as.integer(names(sort(table(v), decreasing = TRUE))[1])
  }, integer(1))
  if (anyNA(landed)) return(NA_character_)
  paste(vapply(split(emp_ids, landed), paste, character(1), collapse = "+"),
        collapse = " | ")
}, character(1))
merge_pattern <- merge_pattern[!is.na(merge_pattern)]

cat("Bootstraps returning fewer than", ega_result$n.dim, "communities:",
    length(fewer), "of", boot_ega$iter, "\n\n")
if (length(merge_pattern)) {
  cat("Which empirical communities merged (a '+' joins the merged pair):\n")
  print(sort(table(merge_pattern), decreasing = TRUE))
} else {
  cat("No sub-dimensional bootstraps to summarize.\n")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: boot-drop-bridge

# The merge above is carried by a single node. MTLD is the only variable in the
# battery with a substantial loading on two communities, positive on the lexical
# one and negative on the cohesion one, and its overlap with content word
# overlap is the strongest cross-community pair in the UVA screen. Holding it
# out tests whether it is what holds the two communities together.
#
# A second bootEGA, so this costs about as much as the one above.
bridge <- "mtld"
stopifnot(bridge %in% names(df_net))
df_nobridge <- df_net[, setdiff(names(df_net), bridge)]

# Holding a node out can move the empirical solution itself, so the reduced
# battery gets its own EGA. Without it there is nothing to read the reduced
# bootstrap against, and P(k) taken from the FULL battery's community count
# would be scoring two different targets with one number.
ega_nobridge <- EGA(df_nobridge, corr = "spearman", model = "glasso",
                    algorithm = "walktrap", na.data = "pairwise",
                    plot.EGA = FALSE)

set.seed(42)
boot_ega_nobridge <- bootEGA(df_nobridge, iter = 500, corr = "spearman",
                             model = "glasso", algorithm = "walktrap",
                             na.data = "pairwise", type = "parametric",
                             verbose = FALSE)

# $frequency is a two-column data frame of (# of Factors, Frequency).
prop_dim <- function(b, k) {
  f <- b$frequency
  hit <- which(f[[1]] == k)
  if (length(hit)) f[[2]][hit[1]] else 0
}

cat("Full battery, empirical n.dim =", ega_result$n.dim, "\n")
print(round(boot_ega$frequency, 3))
cat("\nHolding out ", bridge, ", empirical n.dim = ", ega_nobridge$n.dim, "\n", sep = "")
print(round(boot_ega_nobridge$frequency, 3))

# Each battery scored against its own empirical solution.
cat(sprintf("\nStability of each battery's own solution:\n  full battery      P(%d) = %.3f\n  without %-8s  P(%d) = %.3f\n",
            ega_result$n.dim, prop_dim(boot_ega, ega_result$n.dim),
            bridge, ega_nobridge$n.dim,
            prop_dim(boot_ega_nobridge, ega_nobridge$n.dim)))
```


**Interpretation guidelines** (Epskamp et al., 2018)

- CS ≥ 0.50 means centrality is stable and interpretable
- CS ≥ 0.25 is the acceptable minimum
- CS < 0.25 means centrality should **not** be interpreted

# Section 8. Between-Community Loadings (Bridge Behavior)

Bridge behavior is operationalized via **between-community (cross-)loadings**
from the revised network loadings (Christensen et al., 2025).

```{r}
#| label: cross-loadings
#| tbl-cap: "Between-community (cross-)loadings"

# `nl` (standardized network loadings, nodes x communities) is computed in
# Section 6. What matters is a node's loading on its OWN community against its
# loadings on the others. High and roughly-equal cross-loadings mean
# integrative bridge behavior, a single dominant loading means the node
# belongs to one community.
# nl's columns are named by community id ("1","2",...), matching ega_result$wc.

assigned <- ega_result$wc  # community per node

cross_load_summary <- function(node) {
  row <- nl[node, ]
  own <- as.character(assigned[node])
  others <- setdiff(names(row), own)
  data.frame(
    Variable = short_labels[node],
    Own_community = own,
    Own_loading = round(row[[own]], 3),
    Max_cross = round(max(row[others]), 3),
    Mean_abs_cross = round(mean(abs(row[others])), 3)
  )
}

cat("Standardized loadings (nodes x communities):\n")
print(round(nl, 3))

cat("\nPredictability nodes, in-community vs cross-community loading:\n")
print(do.call(rbind, lapply(pred_vars, cross_load_summary)), row.names = FALSE)
```

# Section 9. Network Comparison by Proficiency Level

```{r}
#| label: proficiency-split

# Use single Overall score from public ELLIPSE data.
df_grp <- df_raw
prompt_grp <- df_grp$prompt

# Three proficiency groups in (approximately) equal bins. `Overall` is discrete,
# with 9 levels in 0.5 steps and heavy ties, so the two cutpoints
# are placed at the observed score levels closest to the 1/3 and 2/3 quantiles,
# which yields near-equal bins.
score_counts <- table(df_grp$Overall)
score_levels <- as.numeric(names(score_counts))
cum_prop <- cumsum(score_counts) / nrow(df_grp)
cut_low  <- score_levels[which.min(abs(cum_prop - 1 / 3))]
cut_high <- score_levels[which.min(abs(cum_prop - 2 / 3))]

df_grp$prof_group <- factor(
  ifelse(df_grp$Overall <= cut_low, "Low",
         ifelse(df_grp$Overall <= cut_high, "Mid", "High")),
  levels = c("Low", "Mid", "High")
)
prof_levels <- levels(df_grp$prof_group)

cat("Cutpoints on Overall: Low <=", cut_low, "| Mid <=", cut_high, "| High >", cut_high, "\n\n")
cat("Proficiency group sizes and score ranges:\n")
print(data.frame(
  Group = prof_levels,
  n = as.integer(table(df_grp$prof_group)),
  Min = tapply(df_grp$Overall, df_grp$prof_group, min),
  Max = tapply(df_grp$Overall, df_grp$prof_group, max),
  Pct = round(100 * as.numeric(table(df_grp$prof_group)) / nrow(df_grp), 1)
), row.names = FALSE)

# Same variable set as the full-sample network
keep_vars <- node_order

# Residualize on prompt within each group, exactly as for the full sample
residualize_group <- function(g) {
  idx <- df_grp$prof_group == g
  d <- df_grp[idx, keep_vars]
  pr <- prompt_grp[idx]
  for (var in names(d)) {
    d[[var]] <- residuals(lm(d[[var]] ~ factor(pr), na.action = na.exclude))
  }
  d
}
df_prof <- lapply(setNames(prof_levels, prof_levels), residualize_group)
```

```{r}
#| label: estimate-group-networks

# lambda.min.ratio as in the full-sample fit, so the group networks are the
# same parameterization as the network the invariance test below works from.
nets_prof <- lapply(df_prof, function(d) {
  estimateNetwork(d, default = "EBICglasso", tuning = 0.5,
                  corMethod = "spearman", missing = "pairwise",
                  lambda.min.ratio = 0.1)
})

cat("Non-zero edges per group (of", sum(upper.tri(nets_prof$Low$graph)), "possible):\n")
print(sapply(nets_prof, function(n) sum(n$graph[upper.tri(n$graph)] != 0)))
```

```{r}
#| label: group-network-plots
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Network comparison across three equal-bin proficiency groups. Colour =
#|   full-sample EGA community, shape = theoretical construct; layout, edge
#|   scaling and the |.05| display threshold are shared across panels.
#| fig-width: 18
#| fig-height: 6

# One layout and one edge-width scale for all three panels, so differences in
# the pictures are differences in the networks.
avg_layout <- relax_overlap(
  do.call(averageLayout, lapply(nets_prof, function(n) n$graph)),
  node_vsize
)
prof_max <- max(abs(unlist(lapply(nets_prof, function(n) n$graph))))

plot_proficiency_panels <- function() {
  graphics::layout(matrix(1:4, nrow = 1), widths = c(1, 1, 1, 0.42))
  for (g in prof_levels) {
    plot_network(nets_prof[[g]]$graph, avg_layout,
                 title = paste0(g, " proficiency (n = ",
                                format(nrow(df_prof[[g]]), big.mark = ","), ")"),
                 legend = FALSE,
                 maximum = prof_max)
  }
  draw_network_legend()
  graphics::layout(1)
}

plot_proficiency_panels()
```

```{r}
#| include: false

save_base_fig("network_group_comparison", width = 18, height = 6,
              draw = plot_proficiency_panels)
```

```{r}
#| label: network-compare
#| output: false

# EGAnet permutation network comparison, run for all three pairs of groups.
# Feed the residualized group DATA FRAMES.
# nc$network is a matrix with columns sF (signed Frobenius),
# JSS (Jensen-Shannon similarity), and Total Strength.
# In each comparison the statistic is oriented as `comparison - base`.
prof_pairs <- list(
  c("Low", "Mid"),
  c("Mid", "High"),
  c("Low", "High")
)
names(prof_pairs) <- sapply(prof_pairs, paste, collapse = " vs ")

set.seed(42)
nc_list <- lapply(prof_pairs, function(pair) {
  network.compare(
    base = df_prof[[pair[1]]], comparison = df_prof[[pair[2]]],
    corr = "spearman", model = "glasso",
    na.data = "pairwise",
    iter = 1000, seed = 42
  )
})

cat("=== Permutation Network Comparison (network.compare) ===\n")
for (nm in names(nc_list)) {
  cat("\n---", nm, "(statistic oriented as second - first) ---\n")
  print(nc_list[[nm]]$network)   # cols: sF (signed Frobenius), JSS, Total Strength
}
```

```{r}
#| label: network-compare-edges
#| output: false

# nc$edges is a list of node-by-node matrices: statistic (comparison - base), p.value,
# p.adjusted (BH), M_permutated, SD_permutated. Report edges whose BH-adjusted
# permutation p < 0.05 (upper triangle only), for each pair of groups.
for (nm in names(nc_list)) {
  padj <- nc_list[[nm]]$edges$p.adjusted
  stat <- nc_list[[nm]]$edges$statistic
  ut <- which(upper.tri(padj) & padj < 0.05, arr.ind = TRUE)
  cat("\n---", nm, "per-edge differences (BH-adjusted p < 0.05) ---\n")
  if (nrow(ut) > 0) {
    sig_edges <- data.frame(
      Node1 = short_labels[rownames(padj)[ut[, "row"]]],
      Node2 = short_labels[colnames(padj)[ut[, "col"]]],
      Statistic = round(stat[ut], 3),
      p_adjusted = round(padj[ut], 3)
    ) %>% arrange(p_adjusted)
    print(sig_edges, row.names = FALSE)
  } else {
    cat("No individual edges differ after BH correction.\n")
  }
}
```

```{r}
#| label: invariance
#| eval: true

# loadings-based permutation invariance test (Jamison, Christensen & Golino, 2024)
# Alternative/supplement to network.compare above if RQ4 is framed as invariance.
# invariance() takes all three groups at once and reports every pairwise contrast.
#
# `structure` is supplied from the full-sample EGA rather than left at NULL.
# With structure = NULL, invariance() runs its own bootEGA on the pooled data
# and silently drops every node whose item stability falls below
# configural.threshold = 0.7. Here that removed the three cohesion nodes, whose
# stability sits near .63, so the cohesion community never entered the test.
# Supplying the structure skips the configural step, keeps the full
# battery, and tests loadings against the same partition used everywhere else in
# this notebook. The tradeoff is that configural invariance is now assumed
# rather than tested.
#
# model and algorithm are passed explicitly because the invariance() defaults
# are BGGM and leiden, not the glasso and walktrap used for the main network.

inv_data <- do.call(rbind, df_prof)
inv_structure <- ega_result$wc[colnames(inv_data)]
stopifnot(!anyNA(inv_structure))

inv <- invariance(
  data = inv_data,
  groups = rep(prof_levels, sapply(df_prof, nrow)),
  structure = inv_structure,
  model = "glasso", algorithm = "walktrap",
  corr = "spearman", na.data = "pairwise", iter = 1000, seed = 42
)

# inv$results is a list with one data frame per pairwise contrast; every
# contrast covers the same node set, so the first one is enough to count.
inv_first  <- if (is.data.frame(inv$results)) inv$results else inv$results[[1]]
inv_tested <- rownames(inv_first)
cat("Nodes entering the invariance test:", length(inv_tested),
    "of", ncol(inv_data), "\n")
if (length(inv_tested) < ncol(inv_data)) {
  cat("Excluded:", paste(setdiff(colnames(inv_data), inv_tested),
                         collapse = ", "), "\n")
}
cat("\n")

print(inv$results)   # per-node loading differences + permutation p-values
```

```{r}
#| label: gradation-note
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

# The monotone Low > Mid > High pattern in the table above is the natural thing
# for a reader to attribute to predictability as a whole. It belongs to one of
# the two predictability nodes, so the callout below says which, and is written
# only for the full-battery run where both are present to compare.
if (length(pred_vars) > 1) {
  diffs <- function(v) vapply(inv$results, function(d) d[v, "Difference"], numeric(1))
  # A true minus sign, so the computed numbers match the typography of the rest
  # of the notebook rather than showing an ASCII hyphen.
  fmt <- function(v) gsub("-", "\u2212",
                          paste(sprintf("%+.2f", diffs(v)), collapse = ", "))
  bh <- function(v) vapply(inv$results, function(d) d[v, "p_BH"], numeric(1))

  # The claim about BH significance is read off the table rather than asserted,
  # since invariance() is a permutation test and the p-values move a little.
  graded <- c("log_mean_token_freq", "var_loss")
  n_sig <- sum(vapply(graded, function(v) sum(bh(v) < 0.05), integer(1)))
  flat_sig <- sum(bh("mean_loss") < 0.05)

  cat(sprintf(
"::: {.callout-important}
## The proficiency gradation belongs to `var_loss`, not to predictability at large

Reading the three contrasts in order (Low−Mid, Low−High, Mid−High),
`log_mean_token_freq` (%s) and `var_loss` (%s) both fall monotonically, and %d
of those six differences survive BH correction. `mean_loss` (%s) is flat, with
%d of three significant.

Holding `var_loss` out does not hand the gradation to `mean_loss`. In
`sensitivity/network-no-varloss.qmd` its three differences are −0.03, −0.08 and
−0.05, so the sign reverses to Low < High and nothing survives BH correction.

The two predictability nodes are redundant in level (wTO = .52, Spearman .81)
but they are not interchangeable across proficiency. Whatever weakens the
loading of `var_loss` on this community as proficiency rises leaves `mean_loss`
invariant. That is an empirical reason to keep both, separate from the
theoretical one.
:::\n\n",
    fmt("log_mean_token_freq"), fmt("var_loss"), n_sig, fmt("mean_loss"), flat_sig))
}
```

```{r}
#| label: compare-predictability

# Predictability-focused edge comparison: partial correlation in each of the
# three groups (Spearman group networks) plus the Low-vs-High permutation
# difference test from network.compare (statistic = High - Low, p.value, BH
# p.adjusted).
nc_lh <- nc_list[["Low vs High"]]

pred_edge_table <- function(node) {
  partners <- colnames(nets_prof$Low$graph)
  data.frame(
    Partner = short_labels[partners],
    Low = round(nets_prof$Low$graph[node, partners], 3),
    Mid = round(nets_prof$Mid$graph[node, partners], 3),
    High = round(nets_prof$High$graph[node, partners], 3),
    Diff_HL = round(nc_lh$edges$statistic[node, partners], 3),
    p_value = round(nc_lh$edges$p.value[node, partners], 3),
    p_adjusted = round(nc_lh$edges$p.adjusted[node, partners], 3)
  ) %>%
    filter(!Partner %in% short_labels[pred_vars]) %>%
    arrange(desc(abs(Diff_HL)))
}

for (v in pred_vars) {
  cat(v, "edge weight by proficiency group + Low-vs-High test:\n")
  print(pred_edge_table(v), row.names = FALSE)
  cat("\n")
}
```

# Summary and Interpretation

```{r}
#| label: summary-values
#| echo: false

# Derived quantities for the narrative below (names stripped so inline R prints
# clean scalars).
focal_label    <- unname(short_labels[[focal]])
pred_comm      <- unname(ega_result$wc[focal])
same_comm      <- names(ega_result$wc)[ega_result$wc == pred_comm]
loss_own       <- as.character(ega_result$wc[focal])
loss_own_load  <- round(nl[focal, loss_own], 3)
loss_max_cross <- round(max(nl[focal, setdiff(colnames(nl), loss_own)]), 3)
cent_sorted    <- cent %>% arrange(desc(Strength))
loss_rank      <- which(cent_sorted$Variable == focal_label)
n_nodes        <- nrow(cent_sorted)
mi_same_comm   <- unname(pred_comm == ega_result$wc["amod_mi"])

# The strength rank is redundancy-sensitive whenever both predictability nodes
# are in (see the caveat under Node importance), so the table cell points there.
mod2_cell <- sprintf("`%s` strength rank = %d of %d%s", focal, loss_rank, n_nodes,
                     if (length(pred_vars) > 1) ", see the caveat in section 2" else "")
```

## 1. Community structure (EGA)

EGA detected `r ega_result$n.dim` communities.

```{r}
#| label: summary-communities
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

if (!is.null(drop_var)) {
  cat("This run holds `", drop_var, "` out of the battery.\n\n", sep = "")
}
for (v in pred_vars) {
  cm <- unname(ega_result$wc[v])
  mem <- setdiff(names(ega_result$wc)[ega_result$wc == cm], v)
  cat(sprintf("- `%s` is in community %s, alongside %s\n", v, cm,
              paste(unname(short_labels[mem]), collapse = ", ")))
}
```

## 2. Node importance

`r focal` loads `r loss_own_load` on its own community, with a maximum
cross-community loading of `r loss_max_cross`. As a secondary check, its raw
strength rank is `r loss_rank` of `r n_nodes`.

```{r}
#| label: summary-importance-caveat
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

# Only the full battery has a redundancy to caveat. The cross-notebook ranks are
# quoted rather than computed, since neither sensitivity run is in scope here.
if (length(pred_vars) > 1) {
  cat(
"**That rank is inflated by redundancy.** `mean_loss` and `var_loss` overlap at
wTO = .52, so each raises the other's strength. Holding `var_loss` out moves
`mean_loss` from rank 1 of 15 to rank 2 of 14, into a near-tie with lexical
density and token frequency, and holding `mean_loss` out leaves `var_loss` at
rank 11 of 14 (`sensitivity/network-no-varloss.qmd`,
`sensitivity/network-no-meanloss.qmd`). The community membership and the
dominant loading survive both tests; the top strength rank does not. Network
loadings are the confound-adjusted importance metric here, and they are what the
interpretation rests on.\n\n")
}
```

## 3. Bridge behavior (cross-loadings)

Bridge behavior is read from between-community cross-loadings (Section 8). High
and roughly-equal cross-loadings indicate an integrative bridge node, whereas a
single dominant loading means the node belongs to one community.

## 4. Interpretation relative to CFA hypotheses

  | CFA Model                | Supporting Evidence                                      |
  | ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------- |
  | Model 1 (Phraseological) | Predictability shares the MI community: `r mi_same_comm` |
  | Model 2 (General factor) | `r mod2_cell`                                            |
  | Novel finding            | See community membership in Section 6                    |

## 5. Stability

CS-coefficients and edge-accuracy CIs are reported in Section 7.

## 6. Proficiency group differences (network.compare)

Three equal-bin proficiency groups (Low / Mid / High), all three pairwise
comparisons. Omnibus structural comparison: signed Frobenius (sF),
Jensen-Shannon similarity (JSS), and total strength with permutation *p*-values.
The statistic is oriented as (second group − first group).

```{r}
#| label: summary-network-compare
#| echo: false

nc_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(nc_list), function(nm) {
  m <- round(nc_list[[nm]]$network, 3)
  data.frame(Comparison = nm, Quantity = rownames(m), m, row.names = NULL,
             check.names = FALSE)
}))
knitr::kable(nc_summary)
```
